title: STAT3 induces amygdala apoptosis by regulating the expression of stathmin in the rat model of posttraumatic stress disorder.
authors: Liu, Wenqiang; Liu, Anqi; Yu, Shengxue; Wang, Yufei; Shan, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PTSD大鼠模型中STAT3调控stathmin表达诱导杏仁核凋亡，虽涉及STAT3-DNA结合（分子对接）但核心是神经行为与凋亡机制，非TF-DNA互作建模，AI/物理模拟方法仅简单对接，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stathmin, recognised as the protein associated with the disassembly of microtubules, plays a vital role in the modulation of human fear as well as anxiety responses. However, it is unclear whether stathmin regulates the specific mechanism of disruption of fear-associated memory resulting from posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). This study aims to observe the impact of stathmin on deficit in fear-based memory during PTSD and investigate the underlying mechanisms involved, in order to establish an empirical foundation for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of PTSD. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We used an single prolonged stress (SPS) protocol to induce the PTSD in the rat model. Open field test and forced swimming test were used to examine the anxious and fearful behaviours exhibited by the rats. STAT3/stathmin signalling-related expressions were assessed through immunofluorescence, immunohistochemical, RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Stathmin and STAT3 binding activity was detected by molecular docking. Amygdala apoptosis was detected by TUNEL staining. RESULTS: In this study, while stathmin gene expression in amygdala was significantly downregulated, after 7 days of SPS, activation of STAT3 was observed in the rats' amygdala, accompanied by a notable increase in the apoptosis rate. Consequently, the rats exhibited heightened fear and anxiety responses. However, the above results were reversed after overexpression of the stathmin gene. In addition, following the administration of the STAT3 inhibitor, WP1066, there was a notable reduction in the apoptosis rate, leading to decreased levels of fear and anxiety in rats exposed to SPS. In rats exposed to SPS, administered WP1066, and injected with adenovirus expressing stathmin-targeted siRNA into the amygdala to make the inhibition of stathmin expression partially counteracted the protective effect of WP1066. CONCLUSIONS: The findings above suggest that SPS could potentially modulate the stathmin gene's expression by activating the STAT3 pathway, subsequently leading to apoptosis in amygdala cells. This sequence of events ultimately contributes to the PTSD rat model fear memory impairment.
abstract_zh: 引言：Stathmin，被认为是与微管解聚相关的蛋白，在调节人类恐惧及焦虑反应中发挥重要作用。然而，尚不清楚stathmin是否调控创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）导致的恐惧相关记忆破坏的具体机制。本研究旨在观察stathmin对PTSD中恐惧记忆缺陷的影响，并探讨其潜在机制，以期为阐明PTSD发病的分子机制奠定实证基础。材料与方法：我们采用单一长时间应激（SPS）方案诱导大鼠PTSD模型。通过开放场实验和强迫游泳实验检测大鼠表现出的焦虑和恐惧行为。通过免疫荧光、免疫组织化学、RT-qPCR和Western blotting评估STAT3/stathmin信号相关表达。通过分子对接检测stathmin与STAT3的结合活性。通过TUNEL染色检测杏仁核凋亡。结果：本研究中，在SPS后7天，大鼠杏仁核中stathmin基因表达显著下调，同时观察到STAT3的激活，伴随凋亡率显著增加。因此，大鼠表现出增强的恐惧和焦虑反应。然而，在stathmin基因过表达后，上述结果被逆转。此外，给予STAT3抑制剂WP1066后，凋亡率显著降低，导致暴露于SPS的大鼠恐惧和焦虑水平下降。在暴露于SPS的大鼠中，给予WP1066并注射表达靶向stathmin siRNA的腺病毒至杏仁核，以抑制stathmin表达，部分抵消了WP1066的保护作用。结论：上述发现表明，SPS可能通过激活STAT3通路调节stathmin基因的表达，进而导致杏仁核细胞凋亡。这一系列事件最终促成PTSD大鼠模型中的恐惧记忆损伤。
